title: PPG-ECG HRV paper: the per-epoch arm re-cut from a committed producer, and the jitter model refuted

instrument.arm: per-epoch rMSSD and SDNN bias, the jitter-budget k-fit, the catastrophic split and the budget's status counts
instrument.estimators: each node's OWN exported estimator over its OWN published series on the common absolute epoch grid: PPGDSP.timeDomain(seg, segMask, null, segAdj) and ECGDSP.rmssd(seg, segSkip) / ECGDSP.std(seg). No HRV math is reimplemented and no DSP changed, so no bundle moved.
instrument.reproducibility: two independent full runs of the same command (1033 s and 1256 s) agree to the printed precision on the three descriptive figures cross-checked here (jitter sd median 6.34 ms, per-epoch rMSSD bias +4.2 %, per-epoch SDNN bias +2.6 %), so the arm is deterministic over this corpus

populations.note: the per-epoch population is a SUBSET of the jitter population; a figure from one must not be read against a drop tally from the other

perEpochRmssdBiasPct.estimator: median across nights of each night's median per-epoch bias — the paper's own definition

perEpochSdnnBiasPct.rangeSource: read off the producer's per-night column; the ranges line does not carry SDNN

wholeRecordRmssdBiasPct.note: a DIFFERENT estimator from the per-epoch figure above, and reported beside it for that reason

kFitConstrained.model: rMSSD²_ppg = rMSSD²_ecg + k·σ² per night, a fixed at 1 (the equation the paper writes)

pooled.note: descriptive only; the pooled k is the one value inside the theoretical band [2,6]

kFitConstrained.note: ONE residual sum, three denominators. A published R² that does not name its denominator can be any of these.

kFitFree.model: rMSSD²_ppg = a·rMSSD²_ecg + k·σ², both coefficients fitted
kFitFree.note: a reads ~1, so the paper’s a=1 constraint is not what breaks the fit

withinNightJitterIqrMs.note: the x-spread a per-night fit has to work with; σ² is the only predictor, so this bounds the achievable per-night R² whether the model holds or not

bareDeviceRmssdR2.note: no model in it — the most charitable reading of an unlabelled published R², measured rather than assumed

published.source: papers/ppg-ecg-hrv-validation.html Draft v2, measured 2026-07 on pre-removal bytes

verdict: REFUTED - the paper's descriptive panels re-cut closely (per-epoch rMSSD bias +4.20 % against +4.24 % published, SDNN +2.60 against +2.46, PPI bias +0.01 ms, sensitivity and PPV at ceiling), and its central mechanistic claim does not reproduce under any estimator searched: the equation as written gives k 1.21 and R2 0.088 against the published k 2.39 and R2 0.964, the same residuals give 0.227 and 0.579 under the other two denominators, freeing the reference coefficient gives 0.672 at a 1.06, and the devices' bare per-epoch rMSSD agreement is 0.649. Part of the failure is structural: within-night jitter IQR is 4.82 ms, so this corpus cannot identify a coefficient on sigma^2 whether the physics holds or not. The paper is re-cut to say so and Table 2 is retained as a labelled illustration, not a design target.
limits: single subject, one device pair, every night quiet sleep
the model was never testable on this corpus at full strength: jitter barely varies within a night
three panels are carried from Draft v2 and still have no producer - the ECG detector-validation residuals (2.2), the epoch-level SQI AUC (3.4) and the two negative fiducial results (4)
per-night and per-epoch values are capture records and stay off the repository; this file holds pooled figures, counts, the night count and the date range only
